name: Pennsylvania
agency: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT), Driver and Vehicle Services
permitAge: 16, with parent or guardian consent (DL-180TD); knowledge test and vision screening

teen.supervisedHours: 65 hours, including at least 10 at night and 5 in bad weather; parent or guardian certifies on DL-180C
teen.nightLimit: Junior license: no driving 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. unless with a parent, guardian, person in loco parentis or spouse 18 or older, or for employment, public or charitable service or a volunteer fire company (with documentation)
teen.passengerLimit: Junior license: first 6 months one non-family passenger under 18; then three, unless partly or fully at fault in a crash or convicted of a driving violation; no limit with a parent or guardian in the car; never more than the seat belts
teen.phone: All drivers: Paul Miller's Law, hand-held devices banned while driving, even stopped in traffic or at a light (effective June 5, 2025; $50 fines from June 5, 2026). Texting ban also applies.

notes: Knowledge test: 18 multiple-choice questions, 15 correct to pass (PA driver's manual, Testing).
The 65 hours must be given by licensed drivers 21 or older per DL-180C; secondary sources say a licensed parent, guardian or spouse 18 or older may also supervise. Not used in questions.

School bus (PUB 97): stop for red lights and extended stop arm; failure brings a 60-day suspension, five points and a fine. Opposite side of a divided highway (barriers, guide rails, trees, rocks, streams or grass median): no stop, reduce speed and use caution.
Steer Clear law (since Sept. 8, 2006): move into a lane not adjacent to an emergency response area, or slow down; fines reported up to $250 / $500 / $1,000. Fine amounts not used in questions.
Learner's permit valid one year; renewal rules from secondary sources only.
Spanish: the PA driver's manual page lists a Spanish translation; direct PDF URL not confirmed. Test languages not confirmed.
